title: Kleidos CLA: configuration read by the bot and the recorder (registry/config.json on main)

coverage_from.description: Pull requests merged before this date predate the register and need no coverage record

app_id.description: The numeric id of the GitHub App kleidos-cla, once it exists: an acceptance posted through it is recorded with method web, any other with method comment

signin_client_id.description: The client id of the identity-only sign-in app (a GitHub App with no permission at all), once it exists. A version whose flow is signin is signed through it, and the recorder accepts only a token of this app

retired_signin_client_ids.description: The client ids of sign-in apps that signin_client_id replaced. Nothing is signed through them any more, but the verifier still accepts the entries that were, so replacing the app does not turn them into findings

timestamping.description: The RFC 3161 time-stamping service the recorder asks for a token over every signature, and the roots its tokens must chain to

qualified.description: Whether the service is a qualified trust service (eIDAS art. 42): its tokens must then carry ETSI's best-practices policy and the qualified statement

flow.description: How the site takes the acceptance: comment, kleidos-cla posts the sentence as the signer (version 1); signin, the signer signs in with the identity-only app, the recorder checks that sign-in with GitHub and nothing is posted (version 2 on). A sentence typed by hand is accepted under either

auto_approve.description: Whether the app approves the held fork runs of a pull request whose authors have all signed. Never true on a repository whose workflows can reach a self-hosted runner (registry/README.md)
